serverInfo.name: Simceptor Mock API Server
serverInfo.description: AI-native cloud Mock API server with 40 MCP tools. Create, test, and manage mock endpoints, conditional response rules, stateful session flows, request logs, chaos testing (fault injection), and an AI-powered issue tracker — all directly from your AI coding assistant (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.).

name: Simceptor Mock API Server
description: AI-native cloud Mock API server with 40 MCP tools. Create, test, and manage mock endpoints, conditional response rules, stateful session flows, request logs, chaos testing (fault injection), and an AI-powered issue tracker — all directly from your AI coding assistant (Claude, Cursor, Windsurf, etc.).

scopes.mcp:read: Read access to projects, mocks, and logs
scopes.mcp:write: Create and modify mocks, rules, and projects

auth.description: Connect via OAuth 2.0 PKCE flow. Alternatively, pass a PAT as standard Bearer token.

capabilities: Create and manage mock API projects
Define endpoints with conditional response rules
Dynamic response templates with Faker.js and variable injection
Stateful session management and state history via Redis
Chaos engineering and fault injection (latency, error rate, jitter)
Local webhook relay tunnel for localhost development
Request log inspection, filtering, and debugging
AI-native issue tracker for mock feedback and fixes

tools.name: list_projects
tools.description: List all active mock API projects belonging to the authenticated developer. Returns project IDs, names, and slugs. The slug is used when calling test_mock to hit the engine.

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Create a new project workspace for organizing and mocking API endpoints. Each project gets a unique slug used to route requests through the mock engine at: https://api.simceptor.com/mock/{slug}/{path}. Don't reconstruct this URL by hand for a specific mock — every create_mock/update_mock/get_mock_detail/list_mocks/get_mock_by_slug response includes a ready-to-use `mockUrl` field with the real, complete public URL for that mock.

description.description: Optional description of what this project simulates

userNotes.description: Optional AI Context Notes / instructions for the project workspace (e.g. focus area, goals, or constraints for your AI agent)

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: update_project_notes
tools.description:
Update or set the AI Context Notes for a project workspace. GUIDELINE FOR AI AGENT: this field is for things NO other tool can recover for you (list_mocks, get_issue, get_rule_chaos_status, etc. only return current data/state, never your own reasoning or intent) — if a future session could reconstruct it by calling another tool, it does not belong here. Write or update notes when any of these apply:
1. Intentional 'broken' behavior — a mock/rule is designed to fail or misbehave on purpose (e.g. chaos testing). State this clearly so it is not mistaken for a real bug and 'fixed' later.
2. Cross-mock dependencies — one mock's behavior depends on state set by another (via set_state / stateLookupExpr). Note the relationship so future edits do not silently break the chain.
3. Guardrails — parts of the project that must NOT be touched (e.g. used in a live demo, or a client-facing sandbox) and why.
4. Current focus — what the user/team is actively working on or testing right now, so priorities carry over across sessions instead of being re-derived by scanning everything.
5. Past chaos/test findings — outcomes of latency or failure experiments (get_rule_chaos_status / get_traffic_chaos_status only expose the CURRENT config, not history or what was learned from a past run).
6. Project conventions — naming or structuring rules not obvious from existing mocks, so new mocks stay consistent.
Also call this right after create_project (summarize purpose & architecture) or whenever the user says 'remember', 'pin', or 'note' something. IMPORTANT: this call REPLACES the entire notes field, it does not append — read the current notes (via get_project_context) first and merge, or you will silently erase prior context.

projectId.description: ID of the target project workspace

userNotes.description: The AI Context Notes text to pin on the project dashboard banner

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: search_mocks
tools.description: Search mock APIs across all of the authenticated user's projects by keyword, tags, or HTTP method. Use this BEFORE creating new mocks to avoid duplicates. Results are scoped to the token owner's projects only.

query.description: Search keyword (matches mock name, path, description; also project/collection names)

tags.description: Filter by tags (matches mock, project, or collection labels)

method.description: Filter by HTTP method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE)

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: list_mocks
tools.description: List all mock API endpoints in a project, organized by collections. Returns each mock's ID, name, method, path, response config, its rules, and slugId. Use this to understand what endpoints are already mocked before creating new ones. Set slim: true for a token-efficient response containing only IDs, names, methods, paths, and slugIds, omitting all rules and default response configurations.

projectId.description: Target project database ID (obtained from list_projects)

label.description: Optional label/tag name to filter mocks (e.g. branch name, sprint name, or scenario category)

method.description: Optional HTTP method filter (e.g. GET, POST)

path.description: Optional path filter (matches if mock path contains or equals this string)

slim.description: Set to true to return only basic mock details (ID, name, method, path, slugId) for token efficiency. Default is false.

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: get_mock_detail
tools.description: Get the full detail of a single mock API endpoint, including all its rules, stateful configuration, webhook settings, slugId, and description. Use this before updating a mock to see its current complete state. PREFERRED: provide slugId (the string like 'MOCK-abc123' shown in the UI) — you do NOT need to know the integer mockId. Provide either slugId OR both projectId+mockId.

slugId.description: Slug ID of the mock endpoint (e.g. 'MOCK-5cbb91d3'). PREFERRED over mockId — no need to know the database integer ID. Visible in the UI and returned by list_mocks.

projectId.description: Database ID of the project (only required when using mockId, not needed with slugId)

mockId.description: Database ID of the mock endpoint. Use slugId instead whenever possible.

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: get_mock_by_slug
tools.description: Look up a single mock endpoint by its slugId (e.g. 'MOCK-5cbb91d3') without needing to know the project or database ID. Returns the full mock detail including all rules, stateful config, and webhook settings. Use this when you have a slugId from the UI or from a previous tool call and want the full detail without looping through projects.

slugId.description: The mock slug ID shown in the Simceptor UI (e.g. 'MOCK-5cbb91d3')

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: create_mock
tools.description: Create a new mock API endpoint in a project. IMPORTANT: Always use the 'rules' field to set up conditional response logic (the Rule Engine). The Rule Engine allows ONE mock endpoint to return DIFFERENT responses based on request content — this is the primary way to simulate multiple scenarios (success, error, validation failure, auth failure, etc.) without creating separate mocks. Rules are evaluated in ascending 'priority' order; the FIRST rule whose conditions match wins. If NO rule matches, the mock's top-level responseBody/responseStatus is used as the default fallback. Use the 'stateLookupExpr' and 'stateCaptureExpr' fields to enable stateful simulation (e.g., simulate a database that persists data across calls). If collectionName is provided but doesn't exist, it will be auto-created.

collectionName.description: Collection folder name to organize this mock (default: 'Default Collection'). Collections are like folders.

name.description: A descriptive name for this mock endpoint (e.g. 'GET User by ID', 'POST Create Payment')

description.description: Optional detailed description of what this mock simulates. Visible in the dashboard UI. Helps team members understand the purpose.

tags.description: Tags for categorization and search, e.g. ['payment', 'checkout', 'transaction']

method.description: HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, etc.

path.description: HTTP resource path. Use curly braces for path variables, e.g. /v1/users/{id} or /orders/{orderId}/items/{itemId}

responseStatus.description: Default HTTP status code (used when no rule matches). E.g. 200, 201.

responseBody.description:
Default response body payload (used when no rule matches). Supports dynamic expression placeholders — complete list: {{path.varName}} (URL path variable), {{query.param}} (query string param), {{header.Name}} (request header value), {{body.field.nested}} (JSON body field via dot notation), {{state.field}} (stateful session value, requires stateLookupExpr), {{random_uuid}} (UUID v4), {{random.number:N}} (random N-digit number, e.g. {{random.number:6}}), {{random.alphabet:N}} (random N-char alphabet), {{random.alphanumeric:N}} (random N-char alphanumeric), {{random.date:format}} (dynamic date, e.g. {{random.date:yyyy-MM-dd}}), {{random.date:format:offset}} (date with offset, e.g. {{random.date:yyyy-MM-dd:+7d}}). Supports localized faker generators (name, email, phone, company, city, address, jobtitle, car, price) with locales (ID, JP, KR, US/Global/EN) using suffix (e.g. {{faker.name_id}}, {{faker.address_kr}}), colon arg (e.g. {{faker.city:JP}}), or call (e.g. {{faker.name('id')}}). For price range, use {{faker.price:min:max}} (e.g. {{faker.price:50000:200000}}). Supports default fallbacks using the colon separator, e.g. {{query.page:1}} or {{body.name:Guest}}. Supports JSON array looping: place an '__repeat' key inside any JSON array object (e.g. '__repeat': 5 or '__repeat': '{{body.items}}') and use {{item}} or {{item.field}} to populate variables for looped items. IMPORTANT: In JSON payloads, ALL placeholder expressions MUST be enclosed in double quotes (e.g. "amount": "{{body.amount:100000}}" or "id": "{{random_uuid}}") to ensure valid JSON syntax for UI linters and parsers. Do NOT leave placeholders unquoted. Do NOT include raw newline characters (
) in the JSON payload. NOTE: the tool response includes a `responseBodyWarning` field if this doesn't look like valid JSON structurally (placeholder values aren't known yet, so only structure is checked) — if present, fix the body and call test_mock to confirm before assuming the mock works.

responseHeaders.description: Default response headers as JSON string, e.g. '{"Content-Type":"application/json","X-Custom":"value"}'

delayMs.description: Default simulated latency delay in milliseconds. Useful for testing timeout handling.

webhookUrl.description: Optional: URL to call as outbound webhook after each request hits this mock. Supports dynamic expressions.

webhookMethod.description: HTTP method for the webhook. Default: POST.

webhookPayload.description: Webhook request body. Supports dynamic expressions to forward request data.

webhookHeaders.description: JSON string of headers for the webhook request.

webhookDelayMs.description: Milliseconds to wait before firing the webhook after the response is sent.

stateLookupExpr.description: STATEFUL SIMULATION: Expression to look up a saved session state by key before evaluating rules. The resolved key is used to load state data previously saved by stateCaptureExpr. Once loaded, state fields become available in rule conditions as 'state.<fieldName>' and in responseBody as {{state.fieldName}}. E.g. 'request.body.user_id' → loads state for the given user_id. E.g. 'request.header.Authorization' → loads state by auth token.

stateCaptureExpr.description: STATEFUL SIMULATION: Expression that determines the key under which to save session state AFTER this request is processed. The request body, response body, and any custom variables (stateCaptureVariables) are saved under this key in Redis (TTL: 15 minutes). Can reference: 'request.body.id', 'request.path.userId', 'response.body.token', etc. Pair with stateLookupExpr on other mocks to build stateful multi-step flows (e.g. register → login → get profile).

stateCaptureVariables.description: STATEFUL SIMULATION: JSON object string mapping variable names to expressions. These named variables are extracted and saved alongside the full request/response snapshot. E.g. '{"balance":"request.body.amount","userId":"request.body.id"}' → saved as state.balance and state.userId, accessible on subsequent calls via stateLookupExpr. Each value MUST be an expression starting with one of: request./response./body./query./header./path./state./item./random./faker. Any value that does NOT start with one of those prefixes is stored as a literal string as-is (e.g. '{"status":"pending"}' saves the literal text "pending") — it is NOT evaluated as an expression.

stateInitialValues.description: STATEFUL SIMULATION: JSON object string defining the default initial state values when this mock or session runs for the first time or after reset (e.g. '{"status": "PENDING", "balance": 0}'). Enables deterministic execution and reliable scenario resetting without modifying scenario definitions.

stateScenarioGroup.description: STATEFUL SIMULATION: Optional scenario group name or tag to group and isolate related stateful mocks together.

rules.description: RULE ENGINE: Array of conditional response rules. Each rule defines conditions to match and a different response to return. Rules are evaluated in ascending 'priority' order (1 = highest priority). The FIRST matching rule wins — subsequent rules are skipped. If NO rule matches, the mock's top-level responseBody/responseStatus is returned as fallback. This enables one mock to simulate: success, validation error, auth failure, rate limit, etc. — all in one endpoint. ALWAYS add rules when the endpoint has multiple response scenarios.

items.description: A single conditional rule. Rules are evaluated in ascending priority order. The first rule whose conditions ALL match will override the mock's default response. If no rule matches, the mock's default responseBody/responseStatus is returned as the fallback.

priority.description: Evaluation order. Lower number = evaluated first. E.g., priority 1 is checked before priority 2. Use sequential integers starting from 1.

label.description: Human-readable name for this rule scenario. Shown in request logs as 'X-Rule-Matched' header. E.g. 'Insufficient Balance', 'Unauthorized', 'Success with bonus'.

conditionLogic.description: How multiple conditions in this rule are evaluated together. 'AND' means ALL conditions must match. 'OR' means ANY one condition is enough. Default is AND.

conditions.description: List of conditions that must be satisfied for this rule to fire. Each condition checks a specific part of the incoming request.

field.description:
The request field to evaluate. Use dot notation. Supported prefixes:
- 'request.body.<jsonPath>'     → JSON body field, e.g. 'request.body.user.id'
- 'request.header.<name>'       → HTTP header, e.g. 'request.header.Authorization'
- 'request.query.<param>'       → URL query param, e.g. 'request.query.page'
- 'request.path.<variable>'     → Path variable from URL template, e.g. 'request.path.id'
- 'state.<key>'                 → Value from stateful session (only available if stateLookupExpr is configured)

operator.description:
Comparison operator to apply:
- 'exists'        → field is present in the request
- 'not_exists'    → field is absent
- '='             → exact string match
- '!='            → string not equal
- '>'             → numeric greater than
- '<'             → numeric less than
- '>='            → numeric greater than or equal
- '<='            → numeric less than or equal
- 'contains'      → string contains substring
- 'not_contains'  → string does not contain substring
- 'starts_with'   → string starts with prefix
- 'ends_with'     → string ends with suffix
- 'regex'         → matches regular expression pattern
- 'in'            → value is one of comma-separated list, e.g. 'active,inactive,pending'
- 'not_in'        → value is not in the list

value.description: The expected value to compare against. Not required for 'exists'/'not_exists' operators. For 'in'/'not_in', use comma-separated values.

joinOperator.description: How this condition joins with the NEXT condition in the list. 'AND' = both must match, 'OR' = either is sufficient. Defaults to AND if omitted.

responseStatus.description: HTTP status code to return when this rule matches, e.g. 200, 201, 400, 401, 404, 500.

responseBody.description: Response body to return when this rule matches. Supports dynamic expression placeholders — complete list: {{path.varName}} (URL path variable), {{query.param}} (query string), {{header.Name}} (request header), {{body.field.nested}} (JSON body field), {{state.field}} (stateful session value), {{random_uuid}} (UUID v4), {{random.number:N}} (random N-digit number, e.g. {{random.number:6}}), {{random.alphabet:N}} (random N-char alphabet), {{random.alphanumeric:N}} (random N-char alphanumeric), {{random.date:format}} (dynamic date, e.g. {{random.date:yyyy-MM-dd}}), {{random.date:format:offset}} (date with offset, e.g. {{random.date:yyyy-MM-dd:+7d}}). Supports localized faker generators (name, email, phone, company, city, address, jobtitle, car, price) with locales (ID, JP, KR, US/Global/EN) using suffix (e.g. {{faker.name_id}}, {{faker.address_kr}}), colon arg (e.g. {{faker.city:JP}}), or call (e.g. {{faker.name('id')}}). For price range, use {{faker.price:min:max}} (e.g. {{faker.price:50000:200000}}). Supports default fallbacks using the colon separator, e.g. {{query.page:1}} or {{body.name:Guest}}. Supports JSON array looping: place a '__repeat' key inside any JSON array object (e.g. '__repeat': 5 or '__repeat': '{{body.items}}') and use {{item}} or {{item.field}} to populate variables for looped items. IMPORTANT: In JSON payloads, ALL placeholder expressions MUST be enclosed in double quotes (e.g. "amount": "{{body.amount:100000}}" or "id": "{{random_uuid}}") to ensure valid JSON syntax for UI linters and parsers. Do NOT leave placeholders unquoted. Do NOT include raw newline characters (\n) in the JSON payload.

responseHeaders.description: JSON string of custom response headers for this rule, e.g. '{'X-Error-Code':'INSUFFICIENT_BALANCE'}'.

delayMs.description: Simulated latency in milliseconds for this specific rule. Useful to simulate slow error paths vs fast happy paths.

webhookUrl.description: Optional: If set, the engine will fire an outbound HTTP webhook to this URL when this rule matches. Overrides the mock-level webhookUrl.

webhookMethod.description: HTTP method for the webhook call. Defaults to POST.

webhookPayload.description: Payload body for the webhook. Supports dynamic expression placeholders.

webhookHeaders.description: JSON string of headers to send with the webhook request.

webhookDelayMs.description: Delay in milliseconds before firing the webhook after the response is sent.

failureRate.description: Used when mode='probability'. Probability that this rule fires. Range: 0.0 (never) to 1.0 (always). Example: 0.3 = 30% chance.

maxFailCount.description: Used when mode='sequential_fail'. Number of consecutive requests this rule fires before the next request is allowed to pass through.

behavior.description: What to do when chaos fires: 'error_response' returns this rule's HTTP status/body. 'kill_connection' drops the TCP connection with no response.

resetAfterMs.description: For sequential_fail: milliseconds of idle time after which the counter resets to 0. Use 0 to disable auto-reset (manual reset only).

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: update_mock
tools.description: Update an existing mock API endpoint. Replaces all fields including rules. PREFER add_mock_rule when you only need to ADD a new rule. Only use update_mock when you need to MODIFY or DELETE existing rules, or update top-level configurations. When updating rules, you MUST provide the full updated rules array.

webhookHeaders.description: JSON string of headers for the webhook request.

webhookQueryParams.description: JSON string of query params for the webhook request.

tools.name: get_request_logs
tools.description: Retrieve recent incoming HTTP requests captured by a mock endpoint. Each log entry shows: request headers, body, query params, matched rule label, response status returned, and response time. PROACTIVELY call this after test_mock returns unexpected results (wrong status code, wrong rule matched, or fallback fired when it shouldn't). result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: test_mock
tools.description: Fire a real HTTP request to the local mock engine to verify a mock endpoint returns the expected response. Use this AFTER creating or updating a mock to self-verify correctness. Test EACH rule scenario by sending different request bodies/headers that should match each rule. Check the 'X-Rule-Matched' response header to confirm which rule fired. If the wrong rule fires or no rule fires, IMMEDIATELY call get_request_logs to inspect the matched rule label and request data. After all scenarios pass, call save_request to document each tested scenario in the Playground.

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

tools.name: get_simulator_spec
tools.description: Retrieve the complete reference documentation for the Simceptor simulator. NOTE: All dynamic expression placeholders ({{path.x}}, {{query.x}}, {{header.x}}, {{body.x}}, {{state.x}}, {{random_uuid}}, {{faker.name_id}}, {{faker.name_global}}, {{faker.city_jp}}, {{faker.company_kr}}) are already documented in the 'responseBody' parameter description of create_mock/update_mock — read those descriptions first before calling this tool. Only call get_simulator_spec when you need deeper documentation on stateful simulation or webhook configuration that is not covered in tool descriptions. Recommended workflow: list_projects -> list_mocks(slim:true) -> list_open_issues_for_mock -> get_mock_detail -> add_mock_rule -> test_mock -> add_issue_comment.

result.description: JSON-stringified tool result or structured text response

Labels exist in 4 scopes: PROJECT (attached to projects), COLLECTION (attached to collection folders), MOCK (attached to mock API endpoints), and RULE (attached to individual rules inside a mock). AI agents MUST call this tool first before using the 'tags' filter in search_mocks or the 'label' filter in list_mocks — to discover what tags are actually available. The response groups labels by their scope so you know where each tag is used.

type.description: Filter by label scope. Valid values: 'PROJECT' (labels on projects), 'COLLECTION' (labels on collection folders), 'MOCK' (labels on mock API endpoints), 'RULE' (labels on individual rules). Omit to retrieve all labels across all scopes.
